summary: 格林兄弟的童话集从民间故事搜集计划，逐渐变成全球儿童读物。文章追索讲述者、跨文化的故事来源和编者留下的价值取向，并用多样的解读解释其生命力。
logic: 逐渐进入家庭和儿童书架
追查讲述者与编者的改写
多重解读带来长久流传

paragraphs.brief: 从民间口述到首版童话集
sentences: The Brothers Grimm, Jacob and Wilhelm, named their story collection Children’s and Household Tales and published the first of its seven editions in Germany in 1812.
雅各布和威廉·格林将故事集命名为《儿童与家庭童话》，1812 年在德国出版第一版，此后全书共出七版。
The table of contents reads like an A-list of fairy-tale celebrities: Cinderella, Sleeping Beauty, Snow White, Little Red Riding Hood, Rapunzel, Rumpelstiltskin, Hansel and Gretel, the Frog King.
目录就像童话名角的名单，有灰姑娘、睡美人、白雪公主、小红帽、长发公主、侏儒怪、汉塞尔与格雷特尔，还有青蛙王子。

Drawn mostly from oral narratives, the 210 stories in the Grimm’s’ collection represent an anthology of fairy tales, animal fables, rustic farces, and religious allegories that remain unrivalled to this day.
合集中的 210 篇故事大多采自口头讲述，兼收童话、动物寓言、乡村闹剧和宗教寓言，至今少有能与之匹敌的选集。
paragraphs.gist: 格林兄弟于 1812 年在德国出版首版《儿童与家庭童话》，整部合集收录 210 篇多源自口述的故事，兼有童话、寓言和乡村闹剧。

paragraphs.brief: 学者搜集故事的原始动机
sentences: Such lasting fame would have shocked the humble Grimms.
如此经久不衰的名声，恐怕会让一向谦逊的格林兄弟大为意外。
During their lifetimes the collection sold modestly in Germany, at first only a few hundred copies a year.
兄弟二人在世时，故事集在德国销量平平，起初每年只卖几百本。
The early editions were not even aimed at children.
早期版本甚至不是写给孩子读的。
The brothers initially refused to consider illustrations, and scholarly footnotes took up almost as much space as the tales themselves.
起初兄弟俩不愿配插图，学术脚注所占的篇幅几乎赶上故事正文。
Jacob and Wilhelm viewed themselves as patriotic folklorists, not as entertainers of children.
雅各布和威廉自视为爱国的民俗学者，并未把给孩子提供娱乐当作自己的工作。
They began their work at a time when Germany had been overrun by the French under Napoleon, who was intent on suppressing local culture.
他们开始搜集故事时，德国正遭拿破仑率领的法军占领，拿破仑有意压制当地文化。
As young, workaholic scholars, single and sharing a cramped flat, the Brothers Grimm undertook the fairy-tale collection with the goal of serving the endangered oral tradition of Germany.
兄弟俩当时年轻、未婚，合住在狭小的公寓里，埋头搜集童话，希望保存德国濒危的口述传统。
paragraphs.gist: 格林兄弟最初想在法国占领时期保存受到威胁的德国口头传统，早期版本销量不大，却配有大量学术注释。

paragraphs.brief: 残酷惩罚引起成人反感
sentences: For much of the 19th-century teachers, parents, and religious figures, particularly in the United States, deplored the Grimms’ collection for its raw, uncivilized content.
在十九世纪的大部分时间里，许多教师、家长和宗教人士，尤其在美国，都谴责格林童话内容粗野、不够文明。
Offended adults objected to the gruesome punishments inflicted on the stories’ villains.
受到冒犯的大人们反对故事里施加给恶人的凄惨惩罚。
In the original “Snow White” the evil stepmother is forced to dance in red-hot iron shoes until she falls down dead.
在最初的《白雪公主》中，邪恶的继母被迫穿着烧红的铁鞋跳舞，直至倒地而死。
Even today some protective parents shy from the Grimms’ tales because of their reputation for violence.
直到今天，一些格外呵护孩子的家长仍因故事以暴力闻名而避开格林童话。
paragraphs.gist: 故事中恶人受到的残酷惩罚曾招致家长、教师和宗教人士的批评，例如《白雪公主》的继母被迫穿着烧红的铁鞋跳舞直到死去。

sentences: Despite its sometimes rocky reception, Children’s and Household Tales gradually took root with the public.
尽管有时不受欢迎，《儿童与家庭童话》仍逐渐赢得了读者。
The brothers had not foreseen that the appearance of their work would coincide with a great flowering of children’s literature in Europe.
兄弟俩没有料到，这本书问世时恰逢欧洲儿童文学蓬勃发展。

English publishers led the way, issuing high-quality picture books such as Jack and the Beanstalk and handsome folktale collections, all to satisfy a newly literate audience seeking virtuous material for the nursery.
英国出版商率先推出《杰克与魔豆》等优质绘本和装帧精美的民间故事集，以满足新近识字、希望为孩子寻找有益读物的人。
Once the Brothers Grimm sighted this new public, they set about refining and softening their tales, which had originated centuries earlier as earthy peasant fare.
看到这批新读者后，格林兄弟开始润饰、软化这些数百年前曾是农民消遣的质朴故事。
In the Grimms’ hands, cruel mothers became nasty stepmothers, unmarried lovers were made chaste, and the incestuous father was recast as the devil.
经他们改写，残忍的生母成了恶毒的继母，未婚恋人变得贞洁，乱伦的父亲则成了魔鬼。
paragraphs.gist: 欧洲儿童文学兴起后，格林兄弟发现了新的读者，便软化早期民间故事的内容，例如把残酷的亲生母亲改成继母。

sentences: In the 20th century, the Grimms’ fairy tales have come to rule the bookshelves of children’s bedrooms.
到了二十世纪，格林童话已经占据了孩子们卧室里的书架。
The stories read like dreams come true: handsome lads and beautiful damsels, armed with magic, triumph over giants and witches and wild beasts.
这些故事仿佛美梦成真，英俊少年和美丽姑娘凭借魔法战胜巨人、巫婆和野兽。
They outwit mean, selfish adults.
他们靠机智斗过刻薄、自私的大人。
Inevitably the boy and girl fall in love and live happily ever after.
男孩女孩最终总会相爱，从此过上幸福生活。
And parents keep reading because they approve of the finger-wagging lessons inserted into the stories: keep your promises, don’t talk to strangers, work hard, obey your parents.
父母也乐意接着读，因为他们认同故事里的谆谆告诫，例如要守信、不要和陌生人说话、勤劳并听父母的话。
According to the Grimms, the collection served as “a manual of manners”.
用格林兄弟的话说，这部合集也是一部“礼仪手册”。
paragraphs.gist: 到了二十世纪，孩子们爱读年轻英雄凭魔法战胜强敌的情节，父母也认同故事里守信、勤劳等行为教导。

paragraphs.brief: 讲述者带来的跨国版本
sentences: Altogether some 40 persons delivered tales to the Grimms.
大约有四十人向格林兄弟讲述过故事。
Many of the storytellers came to the Grimms’ house in Kassel.
许多讲述者直接来到格林兄弟在卡塞尔的家中。
The brothers particularly welcomed the visits of Dorothea Viehmann, a widow who walked to town to sell produce from her garden.
尤其受欢迎的是寡妇多萝特娅·菲曼，她常步行进镇卖自家园里的农产品。
An innkeeper’s daughter, Viehmann had grown up listening to stories from travellers on the road to Frankfurt.
菲曼是旅店老板的女儿，从小听途经此地前往法兰克福的旅人讲故事。
Among her treasure was “Aschenputtel” -Cinderella.
她珍藏的故事中就包括《灰姑娘》。
Marie Hassenpflug was a 20-year-old friend of their sister, Charlotte, from a well-bred, French-speaking family.
玛丽·哈森普弗卢格二十岁，是兄弟俩的姐妹夏洛特的朋友，出身于一个讲法语、家教良好的家庭。

Marie’s wonderful stories blended motifs from the oral tradition and from Perrault’s influential 1697 book, Tales of My Mother Goose, which contained elaborate versions of “Little Red Riding Hood”, “Snow White”, and “Sleeping Beauty”, among others.
玛丽的生动故事融合了口述传统和佩罗于 1697 年出版的《鹅妈妈故事集》，其中包括《小红帽》《白雪公主》《睡美人》等的精心改写本。
Many of these had been adapted from earlier Italian tales.
其中许多是从意大利早期的故事中改编的。
paragraphs.gist: 约四十人向格林兄弟讲述故事，其中一些讲述者带来了法国传统，而其中若干故事的版本又可以追溯到意大利。

paragraphs.brief: 德国乡村及中世纪的印记
sentences: Given that the origins of many of the Grimm fairy tales reach throughout Europe and into the Middle East and Orient, the question must be asked: How German are the Grimm tales?
许多故事的渊源遍及欧洲、中东和东方，那么格林童话究竟有多“德国化”？
Very, says scholar Heinz Rolleke.
学者海因茨·勒勒克的回答是，非常德国化。
Love of the underdog, rustic simplicity, creative energy—these are Teutonic traits.
同情弱者、质朴的乡村气息与创造活力，都是日耳曼文化的特征。
The coarse texture of life during medieval times in Germany, when many of the tales entered the oral tradition, also coloured the narratives.
许多故事进入口述传统时正值德国中世纪，当时艰苦粗粝的生活也给叙事染上了色彩。
Throughout Europe, children were often neglected and abandoned, like Hansel and Gretel.
在整个欧洲，儿童常常被忽视和遗弃，如汉塞尔和格雷特尔。
Accused witches were burned at the stake, like the evil mother-in-law in “The Six Swans”.
被指控为女巫的人会被绑上火刑柱，就像《六只天鹅》中那位邪恶的婆婆一样。
“The cruelty in the stories was not the Grimms’ fantasy”, Rolleke points out, “It reflected the law-and-order system of the old times”.
勒勒克指出，故事中的残酷并非格林兄弟凭空想象，它反映了旧时的法律与秩序。
paragraphs.gist: 学者勒勒克认为，故事虽有跨国渊源，对弱者的同情、质朴作风和残酷的惩罚仍映照出德国民间性格及当时社会的现实。

paragraphs.brief: 无确定时空的普遍吸引力
sentences: The editorial fingerprints left by the Grimms betray the specific values of 19th-century Christian, bourgeois German society.
格林兄弟的编辑痕迹显示出十九世纪德国基督教资产阶级社会的特定价值观。
But that has not stopped the tales from being embraced by almost every culture and nationality in the world.
但是，这并没有阻止这些故事被世界上几乎所有文化和民族所接受。
What accounts for this widespread, enduring popularity?
它们为什么能广泛流传并长盛不衰？
Bernhard Lauer points to the “universal style” of the writing, you have no concrete descriptions of the land, or the clothes, or the forest, or the castles.
贝恩哈德·劳尔指出，这些作品的风格具有普遍性，对土地、衣着、森林和城堡都不作具体描写。
It makes the stories timeless and placeless.
这样一来，故事就不受某一时代或地点限制。

“The tales allow us to express ‘our utopian longings’,” says Jack Zipes of the University of Minnesota, whose 1987 translation of the complete fairy tales captures the rustic vigour of the original text.
明尼苏达大学的杰克·齐普斯说：“这些故事让我们得以表达‘对理想世界的向往’。”他在 1987 年翻译的童话全集保留了原文质朴鲜活的风格。
“They show a striving for happiness that none of us knows but that we sense is possible.
这些故事写出了我们对幸福的追求，尽管从未真正体验过那种幸福，我们却觉得它有可能实现。
We can identify with the heroes of the tales and become in our mind the masters and mistresses of our own destinies.”
我们可以认同故事中的主人公，在想象里成为自己命运的主人。
paragraphs.gist: 具体地点和年代被淡化，使不同文化的读者都能认同主人公，并从他们的命运中看见自己对幸福的向往。

paragraphs.brief: 从心理安慰到多重解读
sentences: Fairy tales provide a workout for the unconscious, psychoanalysts maintain.
心理分析学者认为，童话能让潜意识得到锻炼。
Bruno Bettelheim famously promoted the therapeutic value of the Grimms’ stories, calling fairy tales the “great comforters”.
布鲁诺·贝特尔海姆提倡格林童话的心理疗愈价值，称它们是“伟大的安慰者”。
By confronting fears and phobias, symbolized by witches, heartless stepmothers, and hungry wolves, children find they can master their anxieties.
孩子们通过面对巫婆、冷酷继母和饿狼所象征的恐惧，发现自己能够应对焦虑。
Bettelheim’s theory continues to be hotly debated.
贝特尔海姆的理论至今仍有激烈争论。
But most young readers aren’t interested in exercising their unconsciousness.
不过，大多数小读者并不关心自己的潜意识是否在受锻炼。
The Grimm tales, in fact, please in an infinite number of ways, something about them seems to mirror whatever moods or interests we bring to our reading of them.
格林童话令人喜爱的方式数不胜数，读者带着怎样的心情和兴趣去读，总能从中感到某种呼应。
The flexibility of interpretation suits them for almost any time and any culture.
这种解读空间使它们几乎适合所有时代和文化。
paragraphs.gist: 有人认为孩子可借故事里的恶狼和巫婆面对恐惧，这一心理学解释仍有争议，而故事容许多种解读也有助于其流传。

items.en: The Grimm brothers believed they would achieve international fame.
items.zh: 格林兄弟相信他们能取得国际名声
items.why: 作者说如此持久的声誉会令谦逊的格林兄弟吃惊，表明他们当时并未料想到自己的童话会蜚声国际。

items.en: The Grimm brothers were forced to work in secret.
items.zh: 格林兄弟被迫秘密工作。
items.why: 拿破仑统治下的法国势力压制德国地方文化，是兄弟俩开始工作的背景。原文没有说他们必须秘密搜集或编写故事。

items.en: Some parents today still think Grimm fairy tales are not suitable for children.
items.zh: 今天有些家长仍然认为格林童话故事不适合孩子
items.why: 原文说即使到了今天，仍有一些家长因童话以暴力内容闻名而避开这些故事，正对应认为它们不宜给孩子读。

items.en: The first edition of Grimm’s fairy tales sold more widely in England than in Germany.
items.zh: 英国的Grimm童话第一版比德国更广为传播。
items.why: 文中给出了早期德国销量不大的信息，又谈到英国出版商后来发挥的作用。没有同一时期的两国销量，无法判断首版在哪国卖得更多。

items.en: Adults like reading Grimm’s fairy tales for reasons different from those of children.
items.zh: 成年人喜欢看格林的童话故事原因与孩子不同
items.why: 孩子会被故事情节吸引，父母则赞同故事教孩子守信、勤劳等道理。E 段分别写出两类读者继续阅读的不同原因。

items.en: The Grimm brothers based the story “Cinderella” on the life of Dorothea Viehmann.
items.zh: 格里姆兄弟把“灰姑娘”的故事建立在多罗西娅·维赫曼的生活中。
items.why: 《灰姑娘》是菲曼向格林兄弟讲述的故事之一。她是讲述者，文中交代它来自她的故事储备，并未把她本人写成故事原型。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: In paragraph D, what changes happened at that time in Europe?
items.zh: 在D段中，当时欧洲发生了什么变化？
correct: Literacy levels of the population increased.
人口的识字率有所提高。

items.en: What changes did the Grimm Brothers make in later editions?
items.zh: 格林兄弟在以后的版本里做了什么改变？
correct: The content of the tales became less violent.
故事的内容变得不太暴力。

items.en: What did Marie Hassenpflug contribute to the Grimm’s Fairy tales?
items.zh: 玛丽·哈森普弗勒格对格林的童话有何贡献？
correct: She told the oral stories that were based on traditional Italian stories.
她讲述了基于传统的意大利故事的口头故事。

items.en: Heinz Rolleke said the Grimm’s tales are “German” because some tales
items.zh: 勒勒克认为格林故事很有德国特色，因为有些故事……
items.answer: D · tell of the simplicity of life in the German countryside.
items.solution: 讲述了德国乡村生活的简单性

items.en: Heinz Rolleke said the abandoned children in tales
items.zh: 对于故事中遭遗弃的孩子，勒勒克认为这一情节……
items.answer: A · reflect what life was like at that time.

items.en: Bernhard Lauer said the writing style of the Grimm brothers is universal because they
items.zh: 劳尔认为格林兄弟的写作风格具有普遍性，因为他们……
items.answer: H · avoid details about characters’ social settings.
items.solution: 不详写人物所处社会环境的细节。

items.en: Jack Zipes said the pursuit of happiness in the tales means they
items.zh: 杰克·西普斯说追求幸福在故事中意味着他们
items.answer: E · encourage people to believe that they can do anything.
items.solution: 鼓励人们相信他们能做任何事情。

items.en: Bruno Bettelheim said the therapeutic value of the tales means that the fairy tales
items.zh: 布鲁诺·贝泰尔海姆说故事的治疗价值意味着童话
items.answer: B · help children deal with their problems.
items.solution: 帮助儿童解决他们的问题。

pairs: 题目说故事以意大利传统故事为基础，原文把这种关系写作从早期意大利故事改编。
the simplicity of life in the German countryside
rustic 指乡村的，原文用两个词概括题干中的乡村生活质朴。
points: 拿破仑统治下的法国势力压制德国地方文化，是兄弟俩开始工作的背景。原文没有说他们必须秘密搜集或编写故事。
题干问“海因茨·罗莱克在故事里说被遗弃的孩子”。定位句写到“勒勒克指出，故事中的残酷并非格林兄弟凭空想象，它反映了旧时的法律与秩序。”。
clauses: Drawn mostly from oral narratives, the 210 stories in the Grimm’s’ collection represent an anthology of fairy tales, animal fables, rustic farces, and religious allegories ….
“that remain unrivalled to this day”修饰前面的 anthology。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 anthology，再把修饰信息接回主句。
“that the appearance of their work would coincide with a great flowering of children’s literature in Europe”补足 foreseen 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 foreseen 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
